Oral, ATP-competitive pan-FGFR (1, 2, 3,: Oral, ATP-competitive pan-FGFR (1, 2, 3, 4) kinase inhibitor that selectively targets tumors driven by FGFR2/FGFR3 activating mutations or fusions. Pivotal BLC2001 Phase II (87 patients with locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma harboring FGFR2/3 mutations or fusions, post-platinum) showed ORR 40% (CR 3%, PR 37%), mDOR 5.6 months → FDA accelerated approval Apr 2019. Designed to retain potency against gatekeeper (e.g. FGFR2 V564F) and molecular-brake resistance mutations that drive acquired resistance to reversible FGFR inhibitors (pemigatinib, infigratinib). Pivotal FOENIX-CCA2 Phase II (n=103, FGFR2 fusion / rearrangement cholangiocarcinoma post ≥1 prior line including gem-cis) showed ORR 41.7%, mDOR 9.7 months, mPFS 9.0 months, mOS 21.7 months → FDA accelerated approval Sep 2022.

Orally bioavailable PI3Kα inhibitor that: Orally bioavailable PI3Kα inhibitor that selectively binds and promotes degradation of mutant p110α (PIK3CA-mut) over wild-type — improved tumor selectivity vs alpelisib. Orally bioavailable small-molecule inhib: Orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (mIDH1) — selective for the neomorphic R132 hotspot variants (R132H, R132C, R132G, R132L, R132S). Osteosarcoma is the most common primary: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children + adolescents. Bimodal age distribution: adolescent growth-spurt peak (10–20y; long-bone metaphyses) and elderly secondary peak (>60y; predominantly Paget disease-associated or post-radiation). Standard-of-care multi-modal treatment (full Indications pending): neoadjuvant chemotherapy → en-bloc surgical resection (limb-salvage preferred; amputation reserved for unresectable / vascular-bundle invasion) → adjuvant chemotherapy. MAP regimen (high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, cisplatin) is the global standard from EURAMOS-1 (good-responder arm). Histological necrosis ≥90% at resection predicts favorable outcome; poor responders (<90% necrosis) do NOT benefit from intensification per EURAMOS-1. Platinum-refractory (progression on platinum or PFI <1 mo) is even more aggressive — bev combinations preferred. Urothelial post-platinum PD: enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (EV-302) is now 1L standard but for those who progressed on prior platinum without IO, EV mono or EV+pembro (KEYNOTE-A39); sacituzumab govitecan (TROPHY-U-01); erdafitinib if FGFR2/3 alteration. Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any: Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any child / adolescent / young adult should trigger DICER1 germline testing — the proportion of DICER1-positive cases is high (~30-60%, higher in younger and poorly-differentiated cases). Diagnosis in a postmenopausal woman has a lower (though non-zero) DICER1-positive yield. Treatment: fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (USO) with staging for stage IA well-differentiated tumors in young women; total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH-BSO) for postmenopausal patients or high-grade / advanced-stage disease. Adjuvant chemotherapy (BEP — bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin — similar to germ-cell tumour regimens) for stage IC and above, or poorly-differentiated / retiform variants. Androgen excess resolves dramatically post-surgery (virilization symptoms regress but voice deepening may be permanent). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: contralateral ovary US q6-12 months (synchronous and metachronous DICER1-driven SLCTs reported), chest imaging (PPB risk in survivors' offspring + own residual risk), thyroid US, and abdominal-pelvic US.

PDGFRA D842V substitution mutation in advanced or metastatic GIST. The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). NCCN GIST 2025 Category 1 preferred: avapritinib 300 mg PO QD for PDGFRA D842V-mutant unresectable/metastatic GIST. Tissue or ctDNA-based molecular testing of all GIST at diagnosis is standard of care per NCCN GIST 2025. PDGFRA non-D842V exon 18 mutations (e.g., D842del, DI842-843IM): intermediate imatinib sensitivity — these are NOT covered by this RF. The RF fires exclusively on the D842V substitution. Non-D842V exon 18 PDGFRA mutations route to imatinib (ALGO-GIST-1L step 2 default path).

PIK3R1 mutations may sensitize to alpelisib via the same PI3Kα activation mechanism as PIK3CA. No PIK3R1-specific companion diagnostic exists. ESCAT IIB: PI3K pathway activation in EC is targetable in principle; no PIK3R1-selected approved therapy.

POLD1 germline pathogenic variants in th: POLD1 germline pathogenic variants in the exonuclease (proofreading) domain cause PPAP — similar to POLE-PPAP but with a stronger endometrial-cancer signal in women (lifetime endometrial risk ~50% per published cohorts). Phenotype includes attenuated polyposis with early-onset CRC, endometrial cancer, and CNS tumors in some families. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (Lynch-like): colonoscopy q1-2y starting age 20-25, endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from age 30-35 in women (consider earlier given higher endometrial risk than POLE), EGD q3y from age 30, urinalysis q1y from age 30. Tumor ultramutator phenotype (TMB high) suggests immunotherapy responsiveness in advanced disease; pembrolizumab FDA- approved for TMB-H solid tumors. Risk-reducing hysterectomy + BSO after childbearing is reasonable to discuss in POLD1 carriers (analogous to Lynch INTENSIFIED-track decision). ESCAT IIA.

POLE germline pathogenic variants in the exonuclease (proofreading) domain cause polymerase proofreading–associated polyposis (PPAP) — characterized by attenuated/oligo-polyposis (typically <100 adenomas), early-onset colorectal cancer, elevated endometrial cancer risk in women, and characteristic ultramutator tumor phenotype (TMB >100 mut/Mb) with potential immunotherapy responsiveness. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (Lynch-like; per NCCN Genetic/Familial CRC 2025): colonoscopy q1-2y starting age 20-25, EGD q3y from age 30, endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from age 30-35 in women, urinalysis annual from 30 (overlap with Lynch organ spectrum). The ultramutator phenotype in POLE-mutant tumors predicts immunotherapy benefit (high TMB) — pembrolizumab is FDA- approved for TMB-high (≥10 mut/Mb) advanced solid tumors regardless of tissue; POLE-mutant CRC and endometrial benefit appears substantial in small series. ESCAT IIA (predisposition + tumor-phenotype actionability).

PTCH1 (Patched-1) is the primary tumor s: PTCH1 (Patched-1) is the primary tumor suppressor in the Hedgehog (HH) pathway. It normally inhibits SMO by sequestering it; when HH ligand (SHH, DHH, IHH) binds PTCH1, this inhibition is released, allowing SMO to activate GLI1/2 transcription factors. Somatic PTCH1 loss is the dominant driver of sporadic BCC (~90%). Germline PTCH1 mutation causes Gorlin syndrome (Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome): multiple BCCs from early adulthood, odontogenic keratocysts, skeletal anomalies, calcified falx cerebri, and markedly increased medulloblastoma risk (SHH-subtype, predominantly desmoplastic, in childhood). Gorlin syndrome patients are exquisitely sensitive to ionizing radiation (radiation-induced BCCs within field); radiation therapy is relatively contraindicated for BCC treatment in Gorlin patients. Therapeutic implication: loss of PTCH1 in BCC justifies hedgehog inhibitor (vismodegib/sonidegib) for locally advanced/metastatic disease — routine tumor PTCH1 testing is not required because HH pathway activation is universal in BCC.

Gain-of-function mutations disrupt autoinhibition, leading to constitutive RAS/ERK activation. Clinical contexts: (1) JMML: somatic PTPN11 mutations in ~35% — the single most common driver. Critical to distinguish somatic vs germline origin — germline PTPN11 is a very different clinical entity. (2) Noonan syndrome (germline): most common cause (~50%); N308D, Q79R, D61G hotspots. Features: short stature, cardiac defects (pulmonary stenosis, HCM), webbed neck. Very low lifetime malignancy risk beyond juvenile myeloproliferative disease. Parafollicular C-cell origin — secretes: Parafollicular C-cell origin — secretes calcitonin (diagnostic + monitoring biomarker) and CEA (parallel monitoring). RAI is NOT effective (C-cells do not concentrate iodide). Germline RET testing is mandatory at diagnosis — drives: - Prophylactic thyroidectomy timing in kindred (MEN2B: <1 yr; MEN2A C634: <5 yr per ATA risk classification). - Pheochromocytoma screening (plasma metanephrines / urinary catechols annually) — RET drives both MTC and adrenal medullary tumors. - Hyperparathyroidism screening in MEN2A. Therapy: - Localized: total thyroidectomy + central compartment LN dissection. - Advanced / unresectable (calcitonin doubling time <1 yr or structural progression): selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-001 / -531) or pralsetinib (ARROW) for RET-mutant MTC — superior to multikinase TKIs (vandetanib ZETA / cabozantinib EXAM remain alternatives, significant toxicity). - RET-WT (RAS-mutant or other): no targeted option; cabozantinib / vandetanib by default. Calcitonin doubling time <6 months portends very poor survival; <2 yr drives systemic-therapy decisions even without RECIST progression.

Pentagastrin/calcium-stimulated calcitonin historically used; pentagastrin no longer manufactured in many regions. Basal calcitonin >10 pg/mL in MEN2 carrier → strong indication for prophylactic thyroidectomy. After thyroidectomy (prophylactic or therapeutic): post-operative calcitonin used to assess cure (<2 pg/mL = biochemical cure) and detect recurrence (q6-12 month surveillance). Calcitonin doubling time <6 months = aggressive recurrence (worst prognosis). Procalcitonin can replace if assay available. Falsely elevated in renal failure, pregnancy, autoimmune thyroiditis. Patient has a confirmed germline pathogenic variant in SMARCB1 (chromosome 22q11.2) or SMARCA4 (chromosome 19p13.2), defining rhabdoid tumor predisposition syndrome type 1 (RTPS1) or type 2 (RTPS2) respectively. Autosomal-dominant inheritance with near-100% penetrance for early-childhood disease in classic SMARCB1 cases. Cancer spectrum: atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (ATRT) of the CNS with infancy peak, extracranial malignant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) of kidney / liver / soft tissue, small cell carcinoma of the ovary hypercalcemic type (SCCOHT — SMARCA4 specifically), and schwannomatosis in adolescent / adult survivors. The risk window is extremely narrow (peak ATRT incidence in the first 2 years of life) so high-cadence early surveillance is non-negotiable. Prevention-persona confirmed-carrier RedFlag (§20).

Patient-specific autologous polyclonal c: Patient-specific autologous polyclonal cell-therapy product manufactured ex vivo from a fresh resected tumor specimen (typically a single ≥1.5 cm cutaneous, subcutaneous, lymph-node, or visceral metastasis). Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocol: Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocols are myelosuppressive and require strict hepatic / renal monitoring in infants (often <1 yr old). LVEF threshold 55% (not 50%) in pediatric oncology reflects long-life-expectancy sensitivity to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Larotrectinib / entrectinib much better tolerated than cytotoxic in this age group — the organ-dysfunction flag pushes harder toward TRK-inhibitor monotherapy when fusion-positive (which is >90% of cases). For TRK-inhibitor: dose by BSA / weight per FDA pediatric label; hepatic dose reduction required at bilirubin >3× ULN.

Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DI: Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents + siblings. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is a separate (non- DICER1) etiology that shares the Wilms-spectrum abdominal-tumour surveillance protocol (abdominal US q3-4 months from birth to age 7; AFP q2-3 months from birth to age 4 — focused on hepatoblastoma). Treatment: maximal safe surgical resection (nephron-sparing partial nephrectomy when anatomically feasible; total nephrectomy if not). Histopathology after resection is critical — distinguishes pure cystic nephroma (benign-borderline, surveillance only) from cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma (Wilms-spectrum, requires adjuvant chemo per stage) and from progression to anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney (high-grade malignant, requires multimodal therapy). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: chest imaging (PPB risk), abdominal-pelvic US (ovarian, Sertoli-Leydig risk in girls), thyroid US, and CNS imaging (pineoblastoma, pituitary blastoma risk under age 5).
Pediatric infection screening is broader: Pediatric infection screening is broader than adult — include CMV / herpes given immunosuppression on VAC and likelihood of reactivation in neonates / infants. HBsAg+ infants: confirm vertical transmission, consult pediatric hepatology, entecavir / tenofovir prophylaxis adapted to weight. HIV+ pediatric: ART coordination critical — TRK inhibitors (larotrectinib, entrectinib) are CYP3A4 substrates, avoid CYP3A4 inhibitors. Pneumocystis prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) is standard on cytotoxic arm. Surfaces hold via parallel pre-treatment workup.
Pediatric-inspired adolescent-young-adul: Pediatric-inspired adolescent-young-adult protocols dominate in fit <40; >65 mortality from induction toxicity is high. Mini-HCVD + inotuzumab/blinatumomab achieves better tolerability with comparable CR rates.

Pexidartinib (PLX3397), a CSF1R/KIT/FLT3 inhibitor, is FDA-approved (August 2019) for adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) associated with severe morbidity or functional limitations not amenable to improvement with surgery. ILLUMINATE phase III trial (Tap et al., Lancet 2019): N=120 (pexidartinib vs placebo, crossover design); primary endpoint ORR at week 25 by RECIST 1.1 and TTP-MRI. ORR: 38% (RECIST) vs 0% placebo (p<0.0001); 56% by TTP-MRI vs 0%. mDOR: not reached at median 23.1 months follow-up. Clinical benefit rate: 56%. Safety: significant hepatotoxicity (cholestatic hepatitis, including one fatal case in open-label extension); ALT/AST elevations in ~51%; FDA REMS program mandatory. EMA approved for same indication (2020). No biomarker companion diagnostic required — all TGCT patients are eligible based on clinical criteria (symptomatic, surgery-resistant). CSF1R IHC or COL6A3-CSF1 fusion testing is not required for treatment initiation.

Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secr: Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor of adrenal medullary origin; extra-adrenal counterparts (paragangliomas) arise from sympathetic / parasympathetic ganglia (head/neck, thoracic, abdominal). They are biologically and clinically a single spectrum (PPGL); this entity is anchored to the adrenal subset for ICD-10 cleanliness but cross-references SDHx-driven extra-adrenal paragangliomas in prevention workstream notes. Hereditary fraction is the highest known among adult cancers (~30–40%). NCCN and Endocrine Society recommend germline panel testing (RET, VHL, SDHB/C/D/AF2, NF1, TMEM127, MAX, FH) for ALL patients with PPGL — not restricted by family history. This makes PPGL a sentinel disease for hereditary cancer surveillance pathways (RET → MEN2 prophylactic thyroidectomy; VHL → multi-organ surveillance; SDHB → lifetime PPGL + RCC surveillance). Classical clinical triad: headache + palpitations + sweating; many patients present with paroxysmal or sustained hypertension. Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical em: Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical embryonal CNS manifestations of DICER1 syndrome — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing regardless of family history. Distinct from pineocytoma (Grade 1, benign) and pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation (PPTID, Grade 2-3). Treatment philosophy parallels other embryonal CNS tumours: maximal safe surgical resection (gross total resection is prognostically dominant); craniospinal irradiation in age-appropriate patients (deferred under age 3 due to neurocognitive toll); adjuvant high-dose chemotherapy regimens (often COG/SIOP protocols with carboplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, etoposide combinations + autologous stem-cell rescue in high-risk cases). Trilateral retinoblastoma (bilateral RB1-carrier with pineal pineoblastoma) historically had near-uniform mortality; modern MRI surveillance from RB1-carrier diagnosis has shifted some cases to earlier detection with improved outcomes.

Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that: Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that binds penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis, producing rapid bactericidal activity against most Gram-negative bacilli including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, most Enterobacterales, many anaerobes, and selected Gram-positive cocci. Tazobactam is an irreversible β-lactamase inhibitor (penicillanic acid sulfone) that binds and inactivates plasmid-mediated and chromosomal class A β-lactamases (TEM, SHV, CTX-M ESBLs partially), restoring piperacillin activity against many β-lactamase-producing organisms. First-line empiric monotherapy for febrile neutropenia (FN) at most centers per IDSA, ECIL-4, and NCCN guidelines because of pseudomonal coverage, anaerobic activity, and good safety profile.

Pituitary blastoma is the strongest sing: Pituitary blastoma is the strongest single-tumour DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any infant should immediately trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents (>95% pituitary blastomas carry pathogenic germline DICER1). Distinct from far-more- common pituitary adenomas (which are not DICER1-driven and are typically adult-onset). Treatment: trans-sphenoidal or trans-cranial resection (technically challenging in infants — pituitary blastomas are bleeding-prone and locally invasive); adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-VP16-cyclophosphamide-based regimens reported in case series); RT generally avoided under age 3 due to severe neurocognitive + endocrine toll. Hypercortisolism management (medical adrenal blockade, sometimes adrenalectomy) is an essential pre-operative bridge. Lifelong endocrine replacement (hydrocortisone, growth hormone, thyroid, gonadal axis) after curative-intent resection. Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for survivors.

Positive biochemistry triggers MRI abdomen + 68Ga-DOTATATE PET (or I-123 MIBG). Biochemistry directs adrenalectomy / paraganglioma resection planning. ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs curative-intent surgery scheduling in syndromic carriers.

Polyene macrolide antifungal (broad-spec: Polyène macrolide antifongique (spectre large, y compris Mucorales) — formulation encapsulée par des liposomes pour une réduction de la néphrotoxicité
Polyene macrolide that binds ergosterol: Le polyène macrolide lie l'ergostérol dans la membrane fongique, formant des canaux transmembraniques qui perturbent l'intégrité de la membre, permettent une fuite de contenu intracellulaire (potassium, magnésium) et produisent une activité fongicide. L'encapsulation liposomiale dans les vésicules unilamélariennes (~80 nm) donne de l'amphotéricine aux cellules fongiques par affinité ergostérol tout en épargnant les membranes cellulaires des mammifères (qui contiennent du cholestérol avec une affinités amphotericine inférieure), réduisant nettement la néphrotoxicité, les réactions à la perfusion et le gaspillage d'électrolytes par rapport à l'anphotérocine B conventionnelle. Polyfunctional alkylating agent: each of: Polyfunctional alkylating agent: each of three ethyleneimine groups generates an aziridinium intermediate that alkylates DNA primarily at N7 of guanine, producing intra-strand and inter-strand cross-links → DNA replication arrest and apoptosis. Active metabolite TEPA (triethylenephosphoramide, formed by hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B6 desulfuration) contributes equally to cytotoxicity. Highly lipid-soluble — penetrates CNS readily (CSF levels ~100% of plasma), the basis of its central role in PCNSL induction (MATRix), CNS-relapse-risk lymphoma conditioning (TBC = thiotepa + busulfan + cyclophosphamide; TT-BCNU), and intrathecal use for leptomeningeal disease.

Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule in: Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule inhibitor of all three AKT serine/threonine kinase isoforms (AKT1, AKT2, AKT3) within the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway. Suppresses downstream phosphorylation of effector substrates (FOXO, GSK3, TSC2, MDM2, 4EBP1 via mTORC1), reducing proliferation and survival signaling and partially reversing endocrine-therapy resistance in HR+ breast cancer driven by PI3K-pathway alterations. Tumors with activating PIK3CA / AKT1 mutations or PTEN loss (~40-50% of HR+/ HER2- mBC after CDK4/6i) are enriched for response. Pivotal evidence CAPItello-291 (HR+/HER2- mBC after AI ± CDK4/6i): capivasertib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant — overall mPFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo HR 0.60; in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup mPFS 7.3 vs 3.1 mo HR 0.50. FDA approval Nov 2023 (mutation-restricted).

Risk stratification by SITC 2021: - **Low risk** (generally safe to proceed with monitoring): thyroiditis, vitiligo, stable psoriasis, type 1 diabetes — irAE flare mild, manageable. - **Moderate risk** (proceed with specialist input): RA, IBD (Crohn/UC), sarcoidosis, sicca syndrome, psoriatic arthritis — flare rate ~50%; baseline DMARDs often OK to continue (methotrexate, HCQ but NOT high-dose steroids or anti-TNF at start). - **High risk** (strongest caution; consider alternative if available): active autoimmune hepatitis, myasthenia gravis, inflammatory myopathy, neuromyelitis optica — flare can be life-threatening; benefit-risk discussion mandatory. Pulmonary sarcoidosis specifically: ICI-induced sarcoid-like reactions are well-documented (5-7% of patients on ICI), often mimicking disease progression on imaging. Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and f: Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and for multi-day chemotherapy regimens because of long half-life and demonstrated superiority in delayed-phase CINV control vs ondansetron in head-to-head trials (Saito 2009, Aapro 2014). Triple antiemetic regimen for HEC: NK1 antagonist (aprepitant or fosaprepitant) + palonosetron 0.25 mg IV + dexamethasone 12 mg IV day 1, with dex tapered through delayed phase. Akynzeo (netupitant 300 mg + palonosetron 0.5 mg) fixed-dose oral capsule simplifies triple therapy to two pills (Akynzeo + dex) on day 1. Lowest QT signal in 5-HT3 class — preferred when ondansetron contraindicated due to QT concerns or cardiac comorbidity. Minimal CYP-mediated metabolism makes it the safer 5-HT3 choice in polypharmacy patients (e.g., patients on CYP3A4 inhibitors).

Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic HCV (HCV-RNA detectable OR HCV-Ab+ with persistent viremia >6 months) AND no confirmed B-cell NHL diagnosis. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending DAA antiviral therapy (per IND-CHRONIC-HCV-PREVENTION-DAA) as the etiological-cancer-prevention pathway. Evidence for HCV → NHL causation (IARC Group 1): multiple cohort studies show 2-3x increased risk of indolent B-cell NHL in chronic HCV carriers; epidemiology especially robust for MZL subtypes. DAA cure (SVR12) has been associated with reduced NHL incidence in post-treatment cohorts (de-Re et al. and others) and with regression of established HCV-associated indolent NHL (the basis of IND-HCV-MZL-1L-ANTIVIRAL for the treatment persona). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-drive: Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-driven cancer prevention in immunocompromised hosts. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Gating by additional immunocompromise context is deliberate — EBV seroprevalence is >90% in immunocompetent adults globally, so a RF triggered on EBV alone would fire universally and provide no clinical signal.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HCV-NHL-PREVENTION-OPPORTUNITY and RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence over the two individual RFs (higher priority).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-dri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-driven malignancy prevention. Fires on HHV-8 seropositivity in HIV+, transplant, or other immunocompromised host without confirmed Kaposi sarcoma / MCD / PEL. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending immune restoration (ART for HIV+; transplant-immunosuppression rebalance) + mucocutaneous + oral + GI / lymph-node surveillance. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-KAPOSI. MCD and PEL are HHV-8-driven but not yet authored as distinct Disease entities — covered via the prose surveillance rationale in the indication for now. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (existing) — that is HIV-as-RF; this is HHV-8-positivity-as-RF (the co-factor that turns HIV-related immunocompromise into Kaposi risk specifically).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than mono-infection HBV RF — coinfection carries documented accelerated-fibrosis + elevated HCC risk AND a hard constraint on antiviral selection (tenofovir-based ART mandatory; entecavir monotherapy contraindicated). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending tenofovir-based ART (covers both viruses simultaneously) + AASLD HCC surveillance q6mo. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. HIV-driven AIDS-defining malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma via HHV-8 reactivation, NHL, cervical) are covered separately via RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HHV8-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence (higher priority) and the indication enforces tenofovir-based ART selection.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on positive HIV serology in patient without AIDS-defining or HIV-associated malignancy. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending durable ART suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HIV-PREVENTION-ART) + cancer screening cadence (annual anal cytology in MSM/HIV+; q3-yearly cervical Pap in WLHIV; opportunistic Kaposi/oral hairy leukoplakia visual screening). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the canonical HIV-associated NHL. KS, cervical, anal, Hodgkin, HCC are also HIV-associated; covered via screening recommendations in the ART indication rationale rather than discrete Disease anchors (until DIS-KAPOSI etc. land in v0.2-A authoring backlog).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPRC. STU: Prévention-persona RedFlag pour HPRC. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux co-lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on persistent high-risk HPV positivity OR incomplete/absent vaccination in age-eligible individual. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending vaccination (Gardasil-9) and/or risk-group-appropriate screening cadence (cervical: USPSTF Pap+HPV co-test q5y ages 30-65; anal: HRA + cytology q1y in MSM/HIV+/post-transplant). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CERVICAL and DIS-ANAL-SCC. Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and vulvar/vaginal/penile not yet in KB — v0.2-A authoring backlog.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-dr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-driven ATLL prevention. Unlike HCV/HBV/H. pylori, there is no curative regimen — the intervention is surveillance + transmission prevention, not cure. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Geographic context: HTLV-1 endemic regions include Japan (southwest), Caribbean basin, parts of sub-Saharan Africa, parts of South America, Middle East. Ukraine is low-prevalence; this RF is more relevant for diaspora patients or those with travel/origin from endemic regions.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 the: Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 therapeutic-dose lifetime cumulative exposure. Surveillance: CBC q12mo for leukemia signal (sensitivity modest); breast surveillance per general-population USPSTF unless additional risk factors; oral + salivary symptom awareness. Highest-impact preventive intervention is hydration + lemon-juice sialagogue during I-131 administration (reduces salivary gland uptake) — retrospectively non-actionable for prior exposure. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAF: Prévention-personnage RedFlag pour le risque de HCC MASLD/NAFLD. Le MASDS cirrhotique répond au seuil de surveillance AASLD HCC (US ± AFP q6mo). La fibrose avancée non cirhotique est une zone grise — suivi de l'hépatologie plus proche mais pas encore surveillance de routine. Levier actionable majeur : perte de poids + gestion cardiométabolique. STUB en attente d'approbation à deux co-lead par CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confi: Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confirmed-carrier / clinical- diagnostic-criteria-met cohort. Multi-organ surveillance: pediatric ophthalmology q6-12mo to age 8 (optic glioma); whole-body MRI for MPNST surveillance + symptom-driven biopsy of growing/painful/ neurologically-symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas; women: annual mammography from age 30, MRI from age 30-50. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverrini-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Northeast Thailand has the world's highest cholangiocarcinoma incidence (up to 90 per 100K) — attributable fraction in endemic regions exceeds 50%. Geographic context: relevant for Mekong-region diaspora, refugees, travelers, and adoptees. Companion to RF-CLONORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (East Asian liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 heterozygous carriers. PALB2 approaches BRCA2 breast-cancer penetrance and warrants BRCA-style surveillance with annual breast MRI + mammography from age 30, plus pancreatic surveillance (EUS or MRI alternating annually from age 50, or 10 years before earliest PDAC in family) for FDR-of-PDAC carriers per CAPS consortium 2022. RRSO discussion deferred to BRCA-style threshold given lower ovarian penetrance. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anov: Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anovulation endometrial risk. Separated from the broad reproductive RF for clearer routing — PCOS- specific counseling (progestin restoration, metformin, weight loss) is distinct from generic reproductive-history counseling. Symptom-driven endometrial biopsy in any abnormal bleeding ≥6 months of amenorrhea pre-menopausal OR any post-menopausal bleeding. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RA: Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RAD51D heterozygous carriers. Approaches BRCA-level ovarian penetrance — NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50. Breast surveillance: individualised by family history; consider annual MRI in additional- risk subset. Olaparib PARP inhibitor active in RAD51C/D-mutant established ovarian cancer (PROfound + GEN-ALL trials). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haemat: Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haematobium-driven bladder SCC prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifetime urinary surveillance (urinalysis q6-12mo, cytology + cystoscopy for any new hematuria). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL. S. haematobium-driven bladder cancers are predominantly SCC histology (distinct from urothelial / transitional cell carcinoma that dominates Western cohorts) — engine surfaces this distinction in the prevention rationale prose. Geographic context: Ukraine is non-endemic; this RF is relevant for patients with diaspora / refugee / travel / origin history from sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt, Sudan, Yemen, parts of South America.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-defic: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour le syndrome de déficit en SDH. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux co-lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for active to: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour l'usage actif du tabac. Intervention modifiable du facteur cancer-risque d'impact le plus élevé. Voies moteur à la préventionPlan recommandant conseil structuré sur l'arrêt + pharmacothérapie + dépistage pulmonaire TPMD si admissible à l'USPSTF. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux cliniques-Co-Lead par CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracyc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracycline cumulative dose ≥250 mg/m². Cardio surveillance focus (HF / cardiomyopathy); t-AML surveillance overlap covered by separate RF-IATROGENIC-TOPO2-TAML-PREVENTION. Echo q1-5y depending on risk profile (ASCO/COG-LTFU cadence). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending baseline + serial echo + BNP. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-: Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-amines → urothelial bladder cancer prevention. Fires on documented occupational exposure. DIS-UROTHELIAL anchor preferred but using DIS-HCC as fallback if not in KB on this branch. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic E: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ETS exposure (household / workplace ≥10y). IARC Group 1 + US Surgeon General-confirmed cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum. Distinct from active-smoking RF. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure elimination (cohabitant smoking cessation / workplace smoke-free policy enforcement / personal mitigation) + USPSTF screening eligibility check + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic P: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic PPI exposure ≥10y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) indication-review + de-prescription where the PPI is no longer needed (most common scenario), (2) fasting gastrin + chromogranin A in cohort with persistent acid-suppression indication, (3) EGD with body/fundus biopsies in those with elevated gastrin or symptoms; surveillance EGD q3-5y if atrophic gastritis or ECL hyperplasia documented. Anchored to DIS-GASTRIC (gastric NET and atrophic-gastritis-derived adenocarcinoma both gastric-body diseases); NET-specific outcomes carried in indication prose. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic a: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic anti-TNF biologic exposure ≥3y in pediatric / adolescent / young-adult IBD cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) EBV serology baseline in young adults, (2) B-symptom + lymphadenopathy awareness, (3) annual skin examination (synergistic with concomitant thiopurine + UV), (4) periodic shared-decision discussion of combination- therapy step-down where IBD activity allows (anti-TNF monotherapy has favourable cancer signal vs combination with thiopurine), (5) vaccination catch-up (HPV, HBV, influenza, pneumococcal). Severity = minor — absolute attributable risk in anti-TNF monotherapy is small; the meaningful signal is the combination- with-thiopurine HSTCL warning specifically in pediatric / young- adult cohort, addressed via combination-step-down counseling. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS + DIS-HSTCL. STUB pending two-Clinical- Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic i: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic inorganic arsenic exposure via drinking water >10 µg/L (WHO + US EPA MCL). IARC Group 1 carcinogen with established urothelial, lung, and non-melanoma skin cancer etiology. Anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL per task brief; lung + skin surfaced via relevant_diseases. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending water source change / filtration + intensified screening for affected organs. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic o: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic occupational outdoor UV exposure ≥10y in high-UV-index latitudes. IARC Group 1 solar UV. Distinct from broader RF-LIFESTYLE-UV-EXPOSURE-PREVENTION (which covers tanning beds + sunburn history + recreational UV). Anchored to DIS-BCC per task brief (closest skin DIS to UV-NMSC). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending photoprotection counseling + clinical skin exam cadence + patient skin self-exam education + Vitamin D balance. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic p: Prévention-personnes RedFlag for cronic pancreatite → PDAC. La pancréatite héréditaire comporte le plus haut risque (~40-50% vie). STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic r: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic residential PM2.5 >35 µg/m³ annual average (WHO 2021 IT-1). IARC Group 1 outdoor air pollution + PM. Population-attributable fraction modest individually but large absolute burden in high-exposure regions including industrial Ukraine + during war-related fire / debris events. risk_category=occupational is the closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum (§20 ratification pending). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure reduction + USPSTF lung-cancer screening eligibility + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥3y post-transplant immunosuppression cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan with long-cycle surveillance cadence appropriate to the chronic cohort (vs the acute-window EBV-DNA cadence in the new-transplant RF). Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION- PREVENTION (which covers acute / new-transplant window). Both RFs may fire simultaneously in the early-chronic window (1-3y post-transplant) — engine routes to both surveillance tracks, render layer deduplicates overlapping recommendations. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the primary lymphoma anchor (late- onset PTLD histology more DLBCL-like; DIS-PTLD as the canonical early-onset EBV-driven entity). Multiple cancer types listed in relevant_diseases reflect the broad cumulative-risk profile of the chronic cohort. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined: Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined HRT exposure ≥5y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) shared-decision discussion of risk-benefit (vasomotor symptoms, bone-density preservation vs breast / VTE / cardiovascular risks), (2) lowest-effective-dose + shortest-duration principle per NAMS / ACOG, (3) breast surveillance per USPSTF cadence — supplemental imaging not recommended on HRT alone (density-related supplemental imaging is a separate axis), (4) symptom-prompted endometrial workup (any abnormal bleeding → TVUS + biopsy) for women on sequential/cyclic combined or with intact uterus on any HRT, (5) annual GYN exam. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TAMOXIFEN-ENDOMETRIAL-PREVENTION (different mechanism: SERM with partial endometrial agonism). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined low calcium intake + vitamin D deficiency. WCRF/AICR probable-evidence for calcium and CRC; IARC pooled signal for vitamin D status. RCT evidence for supplementation is mixed at population doses — counseling emphasizes adequate intake/repletion not pharmacologic dosing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary counseling + vitamin D repletion + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for cumulativ: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour une exposition cumulative hormonale-contraception ≥10y, axe iatrogène seulement (exposition-comme risque). Voies moteur à PréventionPlan recommandant le co-test VPH selon l'ASCCP / USPSTF, dépistage mammographique adapté à l'âge par USPSTAF, antécédents attentifs des symptômes (trouillard mammaire, hémorragie anormale). Gravité mineure — augmentation absolue du risque faible, effet sur le cancer du sein atténué après arrêt. Distinct de RF-REPRODUCTIVE-OCP-LONG-TERM (consultation équilibrée risque-avantage, voir §20 seau reproducteur). STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux cliniques-Co-Lead selon le CHARTER §6.1 mode dev.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for endometri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer risk. NO routine population-screening tool exists (CA-125 + TVUS not recommended for general or endometriosis screening per NCCN/USPSTF). Counseling: symptom awareness; consider risk-reducing salpingectomy at completed childbearing or at hysterectomy for benign indications; BSO reserved for those with additional risk factors. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for heavy alc: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour l'alcool lourd. Voies moteur à la préventionPlan recommandant conseil structuré arrêt/modération + pharmacothérapie + dépistage approprié du cancer (endoscopie oesophagienne pour la surveillance du cancer du sein à haut risque pour les femmes). STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux cliniques-Co-Lead selon CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high cumu: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour une exposition UV élevée cumulative. Classement IARC Groupe 1 pour lits bronzant (2009). NCCN Mélanome + lignes directrices AAD soutiennent le conseil de protection UV + auto-examen cutané + cadence clinique examen cutanée. Voies moteur à PréventionPlan recommandant la protection solaire + surveillance de la peau. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux-clinique-Co-Lead selon CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high-pari: Prevention-persona RedFlag for high-parity cervical risk amplifier in HPV-positive women. Counseling: adherence to cervical screening per USPSTF/WHO age-and-method schedule; catch-up HPV vaccination through age 45 per ACIP shared-decision; smoking cessation (synergistic risk). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero: Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero DES exposure. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending annual gynecologic exam with speculum + bimanual + careful palpation of vaginal walls (specific technique for DES daughters per ACOG), colposcopy with vaginal + cervical staining for early detection of CCA, cervical cytology / HPV co-test on routine cadence, breast surveillance per age- appropriate USPSTF cadence. Cohort is aging — bimodal-risk window extends past 40y; surveillance does NOT stop at any age cutoff. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-VULVAR-VAGINAL-SCC (closest existing Disease entity for vaginal-tract anchor) + DIS-CERVICAL. DES- associated cancer is histologically clear-cell adenocarcinoma — NOT yet authored as a distinct DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL entity; histology-specific surveillance considerations carried via the indication prose. Future authoring of DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL recommended. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-LONG-TERM-HRMNL-CONTRACEPTION- PREVENTION (post-natal hormonal exposure, exposure-as-cofactor). This is a one-time in-utero developmental exposure — surveillance cohort is closed (no new DES daughters); known existing cohort remains at lifelong elevated risk.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for late-firs: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour la fin de la grossesse + association d'allaitement court. Tailles d'effets individuels modérés; effet cumulatif non trivial. Impossible de modifier rétroactivement le déclenchement primaire (timing des événements reproductifs) — le conseil est prospectif (encouragement à l'allaité maternelle lorsque possible lors de grossesses subséquentes) + dépistage du cancer du sein renforcé. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux cliniques-Co-Lead par CHARTER §6.1 mode dev.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term: Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term combined OCP use ≥10y. Mixed cancer profile — modest risk increase (breast, cervical-with-HPV) AND substantial protection (ovarian, endometrial). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending COUNSELING-BALANCE indication, not unidirectional risk warning. Critical that render layer present full risk-benefit panel. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prévention-personne RedFlag pour une exposition à dose faible à long terme (RA, psoriasis, IBD). Surveillance : workup à faible seuil pour une lymphodénopathie inexpliquée, symptômes B, organomégalie, masse — retrait de MTX + observer 8-12 semaines d'abord (~50% de régression); persistant → workping de type DLBCL. Examen de la peau annuellement. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux co-lead par CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term ≥3y thiopurine (azathioprine / 6-MP) exposure. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) annual whole-body skin exam by dermatologist + aggressive sun-protection counseling, (2) EBV serology baseline check in young adults pre-initiation (avoid initiation in EBV-seronegative young men per ECCO 2019), (3) annual B-symptom + lymphadenopathy review, (4) shared-decision discussion of indication continuation vs alternatives (MTX for RA, biologics for IBD) at year 5, (5) HPV vaccination catch-up where applicable. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS (lymphoma) + DIS-BCC (closest skin-cancer anchor for SCC and BCC). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term ≥5y calcineurin-inhibitor exposure (cyclosporine or tacrolimus). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) annual or q6mo whole-body skin exam by dermatologist (q6mo if any prior skin cancer), (2) aggressive sun-protection counseling, (3) HHV-8 awareness in endemic cohorts + KS surveillance (skin, oral, GI), (4) HPV vaccination catch-up if transplant context, (5) shared-decision discussion with transplant team of switch to mTOR inhibitor (sirolimus / everolimus) in patients with cumulative skin- cancer burden — CONVERT + ProSparc evidence: mTOR-switch reduces new SCC. Anchored to DIS-KAPOSI + DIS-BCC. Distinct from broader RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION-* RFs by drug-class specificity — applies also to non-transplant calcineurin-inhibitor users (psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, nephrotic syndrome). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for low Medit: Prévention-personnes RedFlag for low Mediterranean-diet adhesive. Levier de référence alimentaire de la population - distinct des RF mononutriments (fibre, calcium, viande rouge). PRÉDIMED RCT (crise primaire cardiovasculaire de 2013; analyse secondaire de 2015 du CRC) + signal d'observation EPIC + NHS. Ancré au DIS-CRC parce que les données sur le cancer sont les plus fortes; bénéfice multi-cancéreux encadré dans la logique. Voies moteur vers la préventionPlan recommandant des conseils sur les modèles alimentaires + dépistage des cadences USPSTF par ancre. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux cliniques-Co-Lead par CHARTER §6.1 mode dev.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for low dieta: Prevention-persona RedFlag for low dietary fibre intake (<15 g/day). WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating for CRC. Effect size modest individually but population-attributable fraction non-trivial (low fibre intake is endemic in Western diets). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary counseling + USPSTF-cadence CRC screening. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for obesity (: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour l'obésité (IMC ≥30). Voies moteur vers la préventionPlan recommandant une intervention structurée de perte de poids + intervention chirurgicale bariatrique dans la classe 2/3 obésité + dépistage du cancer par profil de risque élevé par IMC. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux cliniques-Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior alk: Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior alkylator chemotherapy exposure. Median t-AML latency 5-7y post-exposure; cumulative incidence ~1-10% at 10y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending CBC q3-6mo for first 10y post-chemo + low threshold for marrow evaluation if cytopenias appear. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior the: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour les radiations thérapeutiques antérieures. Étude sur la survie du cancer de l'enfant + document du consortium LATE a augmenté le deuxième risque de malignité primaire décennies après la T.T. STUB en attente de l ́approbation de deux Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior top: Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior topoisomerase-II inhibitor exposure. Distinct from alkylator t-AML: shorter latency (2-3y vs 5-7y), characteristic 11q23/21q22 cytogenetics, often APL-like t(15;17). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending CBC q3mo for first 5y post-chemo + low threshold for marrow evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Note: anthracycline exposure also fires RF-IATROGENIC-ANTHRACYCLINE-CARDIO-PREVENTION (separate cardio + t-AML surveillance overlap).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for processed: Prevention-persona RedFlag for processed-meat consumption ≥50g/day. WCRF/AICR convincing evidence + IARC Group 1 classification for CRC. Effect size modest individually but population-attributable fraction non-trivial. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary counseling + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for refractor: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour celiaque réfractaire → Prévention EATL. Incendies sur atrophie villose persistante / clonalité aberrante IEL / RCD2. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux-cliniques-Co-Lead par CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for reproduct: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour les facteurs de risque de reproduction-histoire. Les tailles des effets sont modestes individuellement mais cumulatives significatives. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux co-lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for salt/pick: Prevention-persona RedFlag for salt/pickle-heavy diet. Counseling: reduce to WHO <5 g/day; co-test for H. pylori in high-intake + high-prevalence settings (Eastern Europe, East Asia); diet-quality intervention (Mediterranean / DASH patterns) provides additional cardiovascular benefit. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for sedentary: Prévention-personnes RedFlag for sedentary style de vie / low physique activity. WCRF/AICR cote de preuve convaincante pour CRC + endométrial + protection contre le cancer du sein post-ménopause. Voies moteur vers la préventionPlan recommandant conseil structuré sur l'activité physique selon HHS + lignes directrices ACS. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux cliniques-Co-Lead selon CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for smokeless: Prevention-persona RedFlag for smokeless tobacco. Most modifiable cancer exposure in users; cessation pharmacotherapy (nicotine replacement, varenicline) is effective. Oral examination at every encounter; biopsy any leukoplakia/erythroplakia >2 weeks; visual inspection with toluidine blue or autofluorescence in high-burden settings. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for sugar-swe: Prévention-personne RedFlag pour la consommation habituelle de boissons sucrées. Conseils : eau de remplacement/boissons non sucrés; réduire progressivement si l'arrêt brutal est difficile; évaluer la contribution à la prise de poids + dysrégulation glycémique. RR individuelle modérée mais très courante → grande fraction absolue de population attribuable. STUB en attente de l'approbation de deux Co-Lead par CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for tamoxifen: Prevention-persona RedFlag for tamoxifen exposure ≥5y in women with intact uterus. ~2-7 fold endometrial cancer risk. Primary IO resistance is operationally d: Primary IO resistance is operationally distinct from acquired resistance (PD after initial response >6 months). SITC consensus (Kluger 2020) defines primary resistance as PD within 6 months of IO start. Subsequent options vary by tumor: melanoma — BRAF/MEKi if V600E, T-VEC, TIL therapy at trial centers, IL-2; NSCLC — docetaxel ± ramucirumab, ADC if HER2/TROP2; urothelial — enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab combination remains active even after IO-mono PD per EV-302; RCC — cabozantinib monotherapy or lenvatinib + everolimus. IO-rechallenge is generally not standard but may be considered after >6 months treatment-free + non-PD discontinuation reason.

Primary Sjögren's syndrome (chronic autoimmune exocrinopathy with characteristic anti-Ro/SSA ± anti-La/SSB autoantibodies and histologic focal lymphocytic infiltration of minor salivary glands; EULAR/ACR 2016 classification criteria) in an individual without a current lymphoma diagnosis. The strongest hematologic-cancer risk factor among rheumatic diseases — ~15-20x relative risk for marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma, predominantly arising in parotid and lacrimal glands, with lifetime incidence ~5-10%. Risk concentrated in patients with persistent parotid swelling, palpable purpura, cryoglobulinemia, low C4 complement, monoclonal gammopathy, lymph- node enlargement, or high EULAR Sjögren's Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI). Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) — confirmed by characteristic cholangiographic findings on MRCP or ERCP (multifocal intra-/extra- hepatic biliary strictures with intervening dilatation, beaded appearance) and/or liver biopsy (concentric periductal fibrosis, onion-skin pattern). Includes PSC-IBD subgroup (very high risk for both CRC and cholangiocarcinoma) and PSC with dominant biliary stricture (additional cholangiocarcinoma risk requiring focused diagnostic workup). No current cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, or HCC diagnosis. PSC is the strongest known risk factor for cholangiocarcinoma — lifetime risk ~10-15% (vs ~0.01% in general population); annual incidence ~0.5-1.5% per year. Prodrug hydrolyzed by carboxylesterases: Prodrug hydrolysé par les carboxylestérases en métabolite actif SN-38 (~100-1000× plus puissant que le parent). SN‐38 stabilise le complexe de la topoisomérase-I/ADN clivable, produisant des ruptures d'ADN à un seul fil qui deviennent létales des rupture de double fil pendant la réplication en phase S. SN-38 est glucuronidé par UGT1A1 vers SN -38G inactif; les patients homozygotes pour UGt1A 1*28 (variante de Gilbert-syndrome) ou *6 présentent une clairance diminuée et une neutropénie sévère + risque de diarrhée — le CPIC et l'étiquette de la FDA recommandent tous deux des tests avant une administration à haute dose.
Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B: Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B6 activation to 4-hydroxy- ifosfamide, which decomposes to ifosforamide mustard — the active DNA- alkylating species producing N7-guanine inter-strand crosslinks and apoptosis in proliferating cells. Side-chain oxidation also generates acrolein (urotoxic — drives hemorrhagic cystitis, neutralized by mesna) and chloroacetaldehyde (the principal neurotoxic metabolite responsible for ifosfamide-induced encephalopathy).
Prodrug that is acid-activated in the pa: Prodrug that is acid-activated in the parietal cell secretory canaliculus to a sulfenamide cation, which forms a covalent disulfide bond with cysteine residues of the H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump) and irreversibly inhibits gastric acid secretion. New pump synthesis is required for recovery (≥24 h half-life of effect despite ~1 h plasma half-life). Cancer-prevention relevance: profound gastric acid suppression is required for H. pylori antimicrobial efficacy (clarithromycin and amoxicillin both require near-neutral gastric pH for stability and bactericidal activity) — PPI is the linchpin of triple / quadruple H. pylori eradication regimens.

Provides supplemental elemental calcium: Provides supplemental elemental calcium (~40% by mass of calcium carbonate). Absorbed in proximal small bowel via active vitamin-D- dependent transcellular transport (saturable at low calcium intake) and passive paracellular diffusion (linear with concentration). Cancer-prevention rationale: intraluminal calcium binds free bile acids and free fatty acids in the colon, reducing their proliferative and pro-inflammatory effect on colonic mucosa; additionally calcium modulates epithelial cell proliferation/differentiation via the calcium-sensing receptor. Calcium Polyp Prevention Study (Baron NEJM 1999) and follow-on trials: 1200 mg/day elemental calcium reduced metachronous adenoma recurrence by ~15-20%.

Pyrexia (especially dabrafenib + trameti: Pyrexia (especially dabrafenib + trametinib) is the dominant BRAF+MEK toxicity — patient education + dose-hold algorithm essential. Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly conve: Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly converted to FdUMP, FdUTP, and FUTP. FdUMP forms a stable ternary complex with thymidylate synthase (TS) + reduced folate (leucovorin), depleting dTMP and blocking DNA synthesis. FUTP misincorporation into RNA disrupts pre-mRNA processing; FdUTP misincorporation into DNA produces strand breaks. Backbone of FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX, FLOT, and capecitabine-bridged regimens. Bolus and continuous-infusion (CIV) schedules differ in toxicity profile (more myelosuppression with bolus, more mucositis/HFS with CIV).
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporate: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporated into DNA and RNA, inhibits DNA methyltransferases → re-expression of silenced tumor-suppressor genes + cytotoxicity at higher doses. Backbone of MDS-HR, AML-unfit (with venetoclax), and CMML 1L therapy.
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycyt: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycytidine. Phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase (rate-limiting) to active metabolites gemcitabine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and triphosphate (dFdCTP). dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depleting deoxynucleotide pools required for DNA synthesis (self-potentiation effect — increases cellular dFdCTP). dFdCTP is incorporated into DNA, after which one additional natural nucleotide is added before DNA polymerase stalls — "masked chain termination" — making the lesion resistant to exonucleolytic repair. Cell cycle phase-specific (S phase) with G1/S blockade. PDAC backbone (gem-nab-pac MPACT, gem mono in frail), biliary tract cancers, NSCLC, bladder, NK/T-nasal lymphoma (SMILE), Hodgkin / DLBCL salvage (GDP).
Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after: Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after intracellular polyglutamation by folylpolyglutamate synthetase, simultaneously inhibits multiple folate-dependent enzymes critical for thymidine and purine biosynthesis: thymidylate synthase (TS — primary target), dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase (GARFT). The combined inhibition disrupts both thymidylate and purine de-novo synthesis, halting DNA / RNA production and producing S-phase-specific cytotoxicity. Activity is histology-restricted: highly active in non-squamous NSCLC and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM); minimal-to-no activity in squamous NSCLC due to higher baseline TS expression in squamous histology. Quantitative HBV DNA tracks response during nucleos(t)ide-analogue (NA) therapy with entecavir (ETV) or tenofovir alafenamide/disoproxil (TAF/TDF). Effective suppression (HBV DNA <2,000 IU/mL, ideally undetectable) is the primary virologic response endpoint per AASLD HBV 2024 and EASL HBV 2025. Sustained suppression reduces HCC incidence by ~50-70% in CHB cirrhotics (REVEAL-HBV cohort; Wong 2013 meta-analysis). Primary non-response or viral breakthrough (≥1-log rise on therapy) prompts adherence review, resistance testing, and regimen change (rare with ETV/TAF/TDF — high genetic barrier). ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs antiviral continuation/switch decisions and is the primary HCC-prevention lever in chronic HBV.
Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral: Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral suppression over time during chronic-HBV antiviral therapy (entecavir or tenofovir TDF/TAF — first- line nucleos(t)ide analogues per AASLD 2024 / EASL 2025). Distinct from BIO-HBV-STATUS (serology-based screening / treatment-decision gate). Two clinical contexts: (1) Treatment monitoring in HBeAg+/HBeAg− chronic HBV: baseline HBV DNA + ALT + HBeAg + HBsAg → start NA → recheck q3 months for first year, then q6 months. Goal: HBV DNA undetectable on treatment; ALT normalization; HBeAg seroconversion (HBeAg+ patients) or HBsAg loss (functional cure — rare on NA monotherapy, ~1% per year). Virologic breakthrough (≥1-log rise from nadir) prompts adherence review then switch (entecavir → tenofovir if NA-naïve resistance). (2) Prophylaxis monitoring during B-cell-depleting therapy (rituximab, obinutuzumab) or anti-CD38 (daratumumab, isatuximab) in HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients: entecavir prophylaxis baseline → HBV DNA q3 months during chemotherapy and for 12+ months post-treatment; any detectable HBV DNA = reactivation, hepatology consult. Quantitative HCV RNA monitoring during direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy: pretreatment viral load (baseline), end-of-treatment (EOT), and Sustained Virological Response at 12 weeks (SVR12) are the standard treatment-response milestones (AASLD-IDSA 2023; EASL 2023). SVR12 is the evidence-based cure surrogate. Persistent viraemia after week 4 / EOT or detectable viraemia at SVR12 → relapse; switch to a salvage regimen containing sofosbuvir-velpatasvir-voxilaprevir (POLARIS-1). In HCV-associated MZL, lymphoma-response correlates with virologic response (Arcaini 2014; Hermine 2002); HCV eradication itself is first-line MZL therapy for indolent disease per ESMO MZL 2024. ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs DAA regimen selection / continuation decisions and (in HCV-MZL) drives the primary cancer-directed therapy.
Quantitative HCV RNA used to TRACK respo: Quantitative HCV RNA used to TRACK response over time during 8-12 week course of direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens (glecaprevir/ pibrentasvir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir, ledipasvir/sofosbuvir). Distinct from BIO-HCV-RNA which captures the single-timepoint quantitative result; this entry captures the serial-monitoring concept for HCC prevention pathway. AASLD-IDSA / EASL minimum testing protocol: baseline HCV RNA + genotype + cirrhosis staging; on-treatment HCV RNA at week 4 (optional, evaluates adherence/response — undetectable at week 4 = rapid virologic response, RVR; not a stopping rule for modern DAAs); end-of-treatment HCV RNA at completion (week 8 or 12); SVR12 — undetectable HCV RNA 12 weeks after treatment completion = virologic cure (>95% achievable with current DAAs, durable in >99%). SVR12 = primary efficacy endpoint for HCV cure; SVR24 essentially equivalent. Post-SVR HCC surveillance remains REQUIRED in cirrhotic patients (cumulative HCC risk reduced but not eliminated by cure; AASLD recommends ongoing q6-month US ± AFP for cirrhotics regardless of SVR status). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved Aug 2017 for R/R-AML-IDH2 monotherapy (phase 1/2: ORR 38%, CR 19%). 1L combination with azacitidine in unfit patients (AG221-AML-005: ORR 71%). Differentiation syndrome (~14%) — same monitoring + dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade; UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic). IDHENTIFY R/R AML phase-3 did not show OS benefit vs conventional care over all comers but enriched in IDH2-mut who had not received prior HMA. Combination with venetoclax + azacitidine under study. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML: R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML (~20-30% of IDH2-mut AML; ~2-3% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved across both R140 and R172 variants. Some series (Stein et al., Blood 2017) suggest R172K carries lower CR rate than R140Q on enasidenib mono, but still substantial activity. Differentiation syndrome (~14%) and hyperbilirubinemia same as R140Q. Glioma IDH2 R172K is a separate clinical entity (vorasidenib INDIGO trial) — this biomarker is AML-scoped; glioma IDH2 captured under BIO-IDH-MUTATION composite. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R175H is the most common TP53 missense h: R175H is the most common TP53 missense hotspot across all human cancers (~5-7% of TP53-mutant tumors per IARC TP53 Database). Structural class mutant — the R175 substitution to histidine disrupts the DNA-binding domain fold (zinc-coordination region). Beyond loss-of-function (LoF), R175H is a canonical example of mutant-p53 GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (GOF): the mutant protein acquires pro-oncogenic activities (chemoresistance via NF-kB, increased migration/invasion, metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation). Clinical implication: R175H+ tumors generally have worse chemo response than TP53-WT or even other TP53-mut tumors. In AML: TP53-mut (any) including R175H → very poor outcomes with intensive chemo, route to alloSCT or venetoclax-azacitidine + clinical trials. In MM: routes to quadruplet per high-risk cytogenetics composite. Emerging GOF-targeting strategies (eprenetapopt/APR-246, arsenic trioxide for structural mutants) are largely investigational; R175H specifically among the reactivatable structural mutants.
R248 is one of the six most-mutated codo: R248 is one of the six most-mutated codons in TP53 (along with R175, G245, R249, R273, R282). DNA-contact class: R248 sits in the L3 loop and makes direct base-specific contact with the DNA minor groove. Substitution to glutamine (R248Q) abolishes sequence-specific DNA binding while preserving overall fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H). R248Q has well-documented gain-of-function (GOF) activities in mouse models — accelerates tumorigenesis and metastasis beyond simple p53-null. Clinical implications mirror other TP53 hotspots: in AML/MDS routes away from intensive chemo toward venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT; in CLL/MCL/MM contraindicates chemoimmuno or routes to high-risk-cytogenetics regimens. Distinction from R248W (different substitution, also a hotspot) — R248Q tends to retain partial folding while R248W more disruptive; both are pathogenic.
R273 is among the top three most-mutated: R273 is among the top three most-mutated TP53 codons (with R175 and R248). DNA-contact class: R273 directly contacts the DNA major groove via its guanidinium side chain. R→H substitution preserves the thermal stability of the protein fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H) but eliminates specific DNA binding. R273H is one of the best-characterized GOF p53 mutants — promotes chemoresistance via NF-κB activation, drives invasion/metastasis through CXCR4 and RhoA pathways, reprograms metabolism (mevalonate pathway upregulation). Clinical implications mirror the TP53-mutant class: AML/MDS — venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; CLL/MCL — contraindicates chemoimmuno; MM — high-risk cytogenetics composite routes to quadruplet. Notably, R273H tumors are particularly resistant to platinum chemotherapy across solid-tumor types per multiple correlative analyses — relevant for ovarian, lung, esophageal cancer treatment selection.
R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codo: R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codon, often grouped with R248 and R273 as the canonical hotspot ring. Hybrid structural/contact mutant: R282 stabilizes the L1/S3 loop region adjacent to the DNA-binding surface, and R→W partially destabilizes the fold while altering contact geometry. Functional studies show R282W retains partial transactivation activity on a subset of canonical p53 targets (CDKN1A/p21, BBC3/PUMA at reduced levels) — termed "partial LoF" — while still gaining oncogenic activities. Clinically R282W behaves similarly to other hotspots: in AML/MDS poor chemo response → routes to venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; in CLL/MCL/MM high-risk regimen routing. Distinction from full LoF mutants (truncating, splice-site) may matter for emerging mutant-p53 reactivator drugs (eprenetapopt) where residual fold is required — R282W generally considered reactivatable in early-phase trials.

RB1 biallelic loss, together with TP53 loss, is the molecular hallmark of SCLC (~95% of cases have both). RB1 loss is not used to select therapy in SCLC (all SCLC patients receive the same backbone: EP/EC ± atezolizumab/durvalumab); rather, it is a diagnostic characteristic and potential therapeutic vulnerability. RB1 loss renders cells dependent on alternative cell cycle regulators (CDK4/6-independent E2F activation) — this is why CDK4/6 inhibitors have no activity in SCLC (pRb loss negates CDK4/6 inhibition). Investigational targeting of RB1-deficient SCLC: aurora kinase A inhibitors (alisertib — phase II, limited activity); EZH2 inhibitors (tazemetostat — RB1-null tumors may have heightened EZH2 dependence); LSD1 inhibitors; ATR/CHK1 inhibitors (replication stress in RB1-null context). ESCAT IIIB: RB1 loss is diagnostically informative and a conceptual therapeutic target, but no FDA-approved targeted therapy exploiting RB1 deficiency as of 2026.
RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (: RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (pRb), the master G1/S checkpoint regulator. pRb normally sequesters E2F transcription factors to prevent S-phase entry; loss of pRb → uncontrolled cell cycle progression. Clinical contexts: (1) Hereditary retinoblastoma: germline RB1 mutation → bilateral/multifocal retinoblastoma in childhood; lifetime elevated risk of osteosarcoma, SCLC, melanoma. (2) SCLC: biallelic RB1 loss + TP53 mutation defines the SCLC molecular signature (~95% of SCLC). pRb loss by IHC is used in pathologic diagnosis. No targeted therapy for RB1 deficiency per se; SCLC treatment is chemotherapy (EP/EC) ± atezolizumab. (3) Urothelial carcinoma: RB1 alterations in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer; associated with basal/squamous subtype; not currently targeted. (4) Breast cancer: RB1 mutations occur in ~10% of TNBC; RB1 loss predicts resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib) — pRb is the substrate for CDK4/6 that drives cell cycle entry; without pRb, CDK4/6 inhibition is ineffective. Carriers face lifetime ~50% risk of secondary primary cancers (osteosarcoma, soft-tissue sarcoma, melanoma, lung, bladder); cumulative risk markedly elevated after external-beam radiation therapy (EBRT) — modern protocols avoid EBRT to mitigate. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per COG / Children's Oncology Group + International Retinoblastoma Consortium): pediatric ophthalmology with EUA (examination under anesthesia) starting in newborn period — every 2-4 weeks until age 1, then progressive lengthening to monthly → q3mo → q6mo through age 7, annual through adolescence. Cascade testing to all first-degree relatives mandatory. Lifelong secondary-cancer surveillance: annual skin exam, attentiveness to bone pain (osteosarcoma in adolescence/young adulthood), avoidance of unnecessary diagnostic ionizing radiation. ESCAT IIA.

RET mutations are the defining oncogenic driver of hereditary and sporadic MTC: approximately 25% of sporadic MTC carry somatic RET mutations (M918T in ~50% of these), and hereditary MTC (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A/2B, Familial MTC) is driven by germline RET mutations (C634R/W/Y/F in MEN2A; M918T in MEN2B; C611/C620/C630 in FMTC-risk MEN2A kindreds). Radiotherapy contraindicated or declined for early-stage NLPBL (nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma, WHO 5th ed). Major clinical scenarios: (1) Young patient with breast or thyroid field overlap — cumulative RT dose risk of secondary malignancy and cardiac toxicity unacceptable; (2) Prior RT to the involved or adjacent region — reirradiation risks exceed benefit; (3) Patient refuses RT after informed discussion. In all scenarios rituximab monotherapy (4–8 × R weekly) achieves ~94% ORR with ≥70% CR in early-stage NLPBL (Advani 2014, IELSG-37 data) and is the accepted standard alternative. RT remains the default for eligible patients where field is safe and patient consents (stage IA-IIA, ≤2 cm).

Rai (Rai 1975, modified) staging stratif: Rai (Rai 1975, modified) staging stratifies CLL by clinical findings: 0 = lymphocytosis only; I = +nodes; II = +splenomegaly/hepatomegaly; III = anemia (Hb <11); IV = thrombocytopenia (plt <100K). Modified Rai groups: low = 0, intermediate = I-II, high = III-IV. Rai 0 has median OS >10 yr — same observation principle as Binet A. Active disease criteria (iwCLL 2018) override stage; this RF fires only when Rai 0 alone is the picture. Companion to RF-BINET-A.
Rai III-IV (high-risk modified Rai) mark: Rai III-IV (high-risk modified Rai) marks symptomatic disease: anemia from marrow infiltration (Hb <11 g/dL) or thrombocytopenia (plt <100K) by CLL — distinguish from autoimmune cytopenia which warrants steroids first. Median OS pre-targeted therapy was 18-24 mo; modern BTKi or ven+G has transformed outcomes (RESONATE-2, ELEVATE-TN, CLL14). Direction `intensify` flips watch-and-wait default to active treatment branch in CLL-1L. Overlaps with Binet C semantically (cytopenia from CLL).
Raloxifene 60 mg PO daily × 5 years for: Raloxifene 60 mg PO daily × 5 years for breast-cancer chemoprevention in POSTMENOPAUSAL women only per STAR P-2 (NSABP-P2, Vogel 2006). ~38% reduction in invasive breast cancer (vs ~50% for tamoxifen) with lower endometrial-cancer (no agonism) and lower VTE rates than tamoxifen. Preferred over tamoxifen in postmenopausal women with intact uterus or VTE-risk profile. Adds osteoporosis benefit. NOT for premenopausal use or DCIS prevention. Counsel on RUTH stroke signal in patients with documented CHD.

Rare but tumor-agnostic actionable drive: Rare but tumor-agnostic actionable driver. Highest prevalence in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma of lung (~7-27% of KRAS-WT IMA), pancreatic KRAS-WT (~3-5%), and isolated cholangio / breast / sarcoma cases. Zenocutuzumab (Bizengri, MCLA-128) — first-in-class HER2 × HER3 bispecific IgG1 — granted FDA accelerated approval 4 Dec 2024 for advanced unresectable / metastatic NSCLC and pancreatic cancer with NRG1 fusion who progressed on prior systemic therapy. eNRGy phase-2 trial (n=204): ORR 33% NSCLC, 42% pancreatic; mDOR ~7-9 mo. Pan-tumor approval reflects rarity (no head-to-head alternative). RNA-NGS testing critical — fusion missed by DNA-only panels in 30-40% of cases. Clinical practice gap: most KRAS-WT pancreatic / IMA-NSCLC patients still not tested at progression. Trial-Source SRC-ENRGY-SCHRAM-2024 not yet ingested — flag for ingestion chunk.

Trial stopped early at interim analysis. FDA approved sunitinib for pNET May 2011 (same month as everolimus). Continuous 37.5 mg dosing vs the on/off 50 mg schedule used in RCC: lower peak exposure, improved tolerability, maintained efficacy in pNET. Also approved for imatinib- resistant GIST (2006) and advanced RCC (2006).

Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose d: Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone until progression) was the MAIA control arm (Facon NEJM 2019, PMID 30926586) and represents the standard-access first-line regimen for transplant-ineligible NDMM. MAIA control arm outcomes: ORR 75.8%, PFS HR (D-Rd vs Rd) 0.56 (95% CI 0.43–0.73), 30-month PFS ~53.3% for D-Rd vs ~37.8% for Rd. Rd continuous showed superiority over MPT and melphalan-prednisone in the FIRST trial (Benboubker NEJM 2014, PMID 25184863): PFS 26 months vs 21.9 months for MPT. Dose of dexamethasone: low-dose (40 mg weekly = "Ld schedule") is preferred over high-dose (480 mg/cycle); ECOG E4A03 showed equivalent efficacy and better tolerability with low-dose dex in NDMM (Rajkumar LANCET ONCOL 2010). Renal adjustment is critical: lenalidomide is ~80% renally cleared. CrCl 30-60 → 10 mg daily; CrCl <30 → 5 mg daily or 10 mg qod. Myeloma renal impairment often improves with therapy — recheck CrCl monthly and escalate dose when GFR recovers. Second primary malignancy (SPM) risk: CALGB 100104 and IFM 2005-02 documented elevated SPM (MDS/AML) with lenalidomide maintenance post-ASCT; risk applies to continuous Rd as well at smaller magnitude.
